lede: Patrick's Browns won it on a 56-yarder Thursday night, and he's up to third — two weeks ago he was last. Sunday is where Mark's lead gets tested.

beats.text: Cleveland led 21-10, let Pittsburgh tie it, and won anyway when Andre Szmyt hit from 56 and Grant Delpit picked off the Hail Mary. Rodgers threw for 299 and three scores and still lost, sacked five times by five different Browns. That's five straight home wins over Jon, Patrick's first three-game streak since 2023, and a climb from last place to third in nine days.

beats.tag: Mark · The one that could cost him
beats.text: Kansas City at Las Vegas, Sunday afternoon. Both 3-0, Jon owns the Chiefs and Mark owns the Raiders, so a point moves straight from one to the other. Mark leads by two and this is the single game most likely to change that. He also has the Niners against Denver and Baltimore hosting Jon's 0-3 Titans, so the day could go very well or get interesting.

Still on two points. The Rams are favored in Philadelphia against an Eagles team that may be without Jalen Hurts, and the Packers are favored in Tampa against a Buccaneers side starting Jalon Daniels with Mayfield's thumb dislocated. Miami at Minnesota and the Chargers in Seattle are both ugly. Two real chances; he has not converted one since Week 2.

Hurts left Monday night for a concussion evaluation and Philadelphia has gone from unbeaten to beaten by twenty in one week. Anthony has the Broncos in San Francisco as well, which is not where you go to fix a bad stretch. Six points and three teams who have all looked worse than their records.
